knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Luu_2022_antiVegf_mbma"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Luu_2022_antiVegf_mbma"))$description`
* Article (open access): <https://doi.org/10.1002/jcph.2002>

Luu 2022 is a model-based meta-analysis (MBMA) of arm-mean best-corrected
visual acuity (BCVA, ETDRS letters) in neovascular age-related macular
degeneration. It extends the individual-level ranibizumab model of Mulyukov
2018 (packaged as `Mulyukov_2018_ranibizumab`) to four anti-VEGF agents and to
sham arms. It then uses the model for a virtual head-to-head comparison of
every-12-week (Q12) dosing.

# Population

The analysis data set holds 22 randomised trials with 55 monotherapy or sham
arms and 9548 subjects (Luu 2022 Table 2): ANCHOR, BAMBOO, BRAMD, C-10-083,
C-12-006, CANTREAT, CATT, CEDAR, CYPRESS, EOP1003, EOP1004, EXCITE, HAGA,
HARRIER, HAWK, MARINA, MORI, PIER, REACH, SEQUOIA, VIEW 1 and VIEW 2. Trial
length was 4.33 to 104 weeks. Arm-average baseline BCVA was 47.0 to 65.8
letters, with a median of 56.4 letters over the 55 arms. Only aggregate arm
data were used. The paper reports no age, sex or race distribution. Arms with
pro re nata or treat-and-extend dosing were excluded. The two bevacizumab arms
were fitted but could not be simulated, because no bevacizumab half-life or
EC50 was estimated.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Luu_2022_antiVegf_mbma")()$population`.

# Virtual arms

The model describes trial-arm means, so each simulated "subject" below is one
trial arm. The arm list reproduces the regimens and baseline BCVA of Luu 2022
Table 2 for the regimen groups shown in Figure 4. "Monthly" dosing (Table 2
footnote a) is every 52/12 weeks, and Q4 is every 4 weeks.

```{r regimens}
monthly <- 52 / 12
regimens <- list(
  rani_monthly = seq(0, 52, by = monthly),
  q4 = seq(0, 48, by = 4),
  # Three monthly loading doses, then every 3 months (EXCITE, PIER).
  rani_q12 = c(0, 1, 2, 5, 8, 11) * monthly,
  # Three 4-weekly loading doses, then every 12 weeks (HAWK, HARRIER).
  bro_q12 = c(0, 4, 8, 20, 32, 44),
  # Three 4-weekly loading doses, then every 8 weeks.
  q8 = c(0, 4, 8, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48),
  # Loading doses at weeks 0, 4 and 12, then every 12 weeks (Figure 5).
  q12 = c(0, 4, 12, 24, 36, 48)
)

# One row per Figure 4 regimen group: drug, dose (mg), regimen, the baseline
# BCVA of each contributing Table 2 arm, the assessment week, and the
# Figure 4 model-predicted and observed week 48/52 change from baseline.
fig4 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~group, ~drug, ~dose, ~regimen, ~base, ~week, ~pred_paper, ~obs_paper,
  "Ranibizumab, monthly (0.5 mg)", "ranibizumab", 0.5, "rani_monthly", c(47.1, 60.0, 59.5, 53.7, 53.8), 52, 7.42, 7.43,
  "Ranibizumab, monthly (0.3 mg)", "ranibizumab", 0.3, "rani_monthly", c(47.0, 53.1, 56.5), 52, 7.31, 7.42,
  "Ranibizumab, Q4 (0.5 mg)", "ranibizumab", 0.5, "q4", c(60.1, 56.4, 57.0, 54.0), 52, 8.70, 8.59,
  "Ranibizumab, Q12 (0.5 mg)", "ranibizumab", 0.5, "rani_q12", c(57.7, 53.7), 52, 2.77, 1.78,
  "Ranibizumab, Q12 (0.3 mg)", "ranibizumab", 0.3, "rani_q12", c(55.8, 55.8), 52, 2.31, 2.13,
  "Brolucizumab, Q12/Q8 (6 mg)", "brolucizumab", 6, "bro_q12", c(60.8, 61.5), 48, 6.74, 6.75,
  "Brolucizumab, Q12/Q8 (3 mg)", "brolucizumab", 3, "bro_q12", c(61.0), 48, 6.23, 6.10,
  "Aflibercept, Q8 (2 mg)", "aflibercept", 2, "q8", c(55.7, 51.6, 60.0, 60.8, 63.1, 65.8), 52, 7.75, 7.83,
  "Aflibercept, Q4 (2 mg)", "aflibercept", 2, "q4", c(55.2, 52.8), 52, 9.06, 9.24,
  "Aflibercept, Q4 (0.5 mg)", "aflibercept", 0.5, "q4", c(55.6, 51.6), 52, 8.44, 8.24,
  "Abicipar, Q8 (2 mg)", "abicipar", 2, "q8", c(56.5, 57.2), 52, 7.47, 7.49,
  "Abicipar, Q12 (2 mg)", "abicipar", 2, "q12", c(56.4, 56.4), 52, 5.92, 6.12
)

# Build the event table for one arm. Doses go into the vitreous `central`
# compartment; observations are on the `bcva` state.
make_arm <- function(id, drug, dose, dose_times, base, week, n_arm = 300,
                     obs_times = c(0, week)) {
  trt <- c(ranibizumab = 0, aflibercept = 0, brolucizumab = 0, abicipar = 0)
  if (drug != "sham") trt[[drug]] <- 1
  doses <- if (drug == "sham") NULL else
    tibble(time = dose_times[dose_times < week], evid = 1L, amt = dose, cmt = "central")
  bind_rows(doses, tibble(time = obs_times, evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "bcva")) |>
    mutate(
      id = id,
      TRT_RANIBIZUMAB = trt[["ranibizumab"]],
      TRT_AFLIBERCEPT = trt[["aflibercept"]],
      TRT_BROLUCIZUMAB = trt[["brolucizumab"]],
      TRT_ABICIPAR = trt[["abicipar"]],
      SCORE_BCVA = base,
      N_ARM = n_arm
    ) |>
    arrange(time, desc(evid))
}

arms4 <- fig4 |>
  mutate(g = row_number()) |>
  tidyr::unnest(base) |>
  mutate(id = row_number())
ev4 <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(arms4)), function(i) {
  a <- arms4[i, ]
  make_arm(a$id, a$drug, a$dose, regimens[[a$regimen]], a$base, a$week) |>
    mutate(group = a$group)
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(ev4[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
mod <- readModelDb("Luu_2022_antiVegf_mbma")
mod_typical <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod, "omega")

# Each simulated id is one trial arm, so a typical-value solve over several
# arms is intended; muffle only rxode2's warning about that.
solve_typical <- function(events, ...) {
  withCallingHandlers(
    rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typical, events = events, ...),
    warning = function(w) {
      if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
        invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
      }
    }
  )
}
sim4 <- solve_typical(ev4, keep = "group") |>
  as.data.frame()
```

# Replicate published figures

## Figure 4: week 48/52 change from baseline on the labelled regimens

Luu 2022 Figure 4 compares, for each regimen group, the observed mean change
from baseline with the mean model prediction across the contributing arms.
The paper's predictions use each arm's empirical Bayes estimates (Results,
p. 600). The library model has no arm estimates, so the values below are
typical-value predictions at each arm's baseline BCVA, averaged over the arms
of the group.

```{r figure-4}
fig4_sim <- sim4 |>
  group_by(id, group) |>
  filter(time == max(time)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  group_by(group) |>
  summarise(cfb_sim = mean(bcva_cfb), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(select(fig4, group, pred_paper, obs_paper), by = "group") |>
  mutate(diff = cfb_sim - pred_paper)
stopifnot(nrow(fig4_sim) == nrow(fig4))

fig4_sim |>
  mutate(across(c(cfb_sim, diff), \(x) round(x, 2))) |>
  rename(
    "Regimen group" = group,
    "Simulated typical value (letters)" = cfb_sim,
    "Luu 2022 predicted (letters)" = pred_paper,
    "Luu 2022 observed (letters)" = obs_paper,
    "Simulated - predicted" = diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Replicates Figure 4 of Luu 2022: mean change from baseline BCVA at week 48 (brolucizumab) or 52.")

# Deterministic typical values. Realised: median |diff| 1.42 letters, mean
# signed diff -0.01, max |diff| 3.16 (ranibizumab monthly 0.3 mg, whose ANCHOR
# arm starts at 47 letters). A tenfold EC50 error or a swapped half-life moves
# several groups by more than 3 letters and the mean by more than 1.
stopifnot(
  median(abs(fig4_sim$diff)) < 2,
  abs(mean(fig4_sim$diff)) < 1
)
```

```{r figure-4-plot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5}
fig4_sim |>
  select(group, `Simulated typical value` = cfb_sim, `Luu 2022 predicted` = pred_paper,
         `Luu 2022 observed` = obs_paper) |>
  pivot_longer(-group, names_to = "source", values_to = "cfb") |>
  ggplot(aes(cfb, group, colour = source)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  labs(x = "Change from baseline at week 48/52 (letters)", y = NULL, colour = NULL,
       caption = "Replicates Figure 4 of Luu 2022.") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Figure 5: virtual head-to-head comparison of Q12 dosing

Figure 5 simulates each drug with loading doses at weeks 0, 4 and 12 and
then every 12 weeks, at the baseline BCVA of every arm of that drug in
Table 2. Doses are the labelled strengths: abicipar 2 mg, aflibercept 2 mg,
brolucizumab 6 mg and ranibizumab 0.5 mg.

```{r figure-5}
base5 <- list(
  abicipar = c(58.5, 54.3, 56.4, 56.5, 55.2, 59.0, 58.4, 58.5, 56.4, 57.2),
  aflibercept = c(55.6, 63.1, 60.8, 60.0, 65.8, 55.2, 55.6, 55.7, 52.8, 51.6, 51.6),
  brolucizumab = c(63.6, 57.9, 56.8, 54.9, 54.1, 61.5, 61.0, 60.8),
  ranibizumab = c(47.0, 47.1, 55.8, 60.0, 56.6, 59.5, 60.1, 56.4, 57.6, 55.8,
                  57.7, 56.5, 53.1, 53.7, 55.8, 53.7, 60.4, 57.0, 54.0, 53.8)
)
dose5 <- c(abicipar = 2, aflibercept = 2, brolucizumab = 6, ranibizumab = 0.5)
arms5 <- tibble(drug = names(base5), base = base5) |>
  tidyr::unnest(base) |>
  mutate(id = row_number())
ev5 <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(arms5)), function(i) {
  a <- arms5[i, ]
  make_arm(a$id, a$drug, dose5[[a$drug]], regimens$q12, a$base, 52,
           obs_times = 0:52) |>
    mutate(drug = a$drug)
}))
sim5 <- solve_typical(ev5, keep = "drug") |>
  as.data.frame()

fig5_paper <- tibble::tribble(
  ~drug, ~mean_paper, ~sd_paper,
  "abicipar", 5.92, 1.02,
  "aflibercept", 3.04, 1.61,
  "brolucizumab", 6.61, 0.284,
  "ranibizumab", 3.02, 2.35
)
fig5_sim <- sim5 |>
  filter(time == 52) |>
  group_by(drug) |>
  summarise(mean_sim = mean(bcva_cfb), sd_sim = sd(bcva_cfb), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(fig5_paper, by = "drug") |>
  mutate(diff = mean_sim - mean_paper)
stopifnot(nrow(fig5_sim) == 4)

fig5_sim |>
  mutate(across(c(mean_sim, sd_sim, diff), \(x) round(x, 2))) |>
  rename(
    "Drug" = drug,
    "Simulated mean (letters)" = mean_sim,
    "Simulated SD across arms" = sd_sim,
    "Luu 2022 mean (letters)" = mean_paper,
    "Luu 2022 SD" = sd_paper,
    "Simulated - Luu 2022" = diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Replicates Figure 5 of Luu 2022: week 52 change from baseline on fixed Q12 dosing.")

# Deterministic. Realised |diff| 0.13-0.66 letters. The paper's conclusion
# that abicipar and brolucizumab keep about 3 more letters than aflibercept
# and ranibizumab on Q12 dosing is checked as a gap, not as an ordering of
# near-equal values.
cfb5 <- setNames(fig5_sim$mean_sim, fig5_sim$drug)
stopifnot(
  all(abs(fig5_sim$diff) < 1.2),
  min(cfb5[c("abicipar", "brolucizumab")]) - max(cfb5[c("aflibercept", "ranibizumab")]) > 1.5
)
```

```{r figure-5-plot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
sim5 |>
  group_by(drug, time) |>
  summarise(cfb = mean(bcva_cfb), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(time, cfb, colour = drug)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = regimens$q12, linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey50") +
  labs(x = "Time from first dose (weeks)", y = "Change from baseline BCVA (letters)",
       colour = NULL,
       caption = "Mean typical-value trajectory across the Table 2 arms of each drug; Q12 dosing as in Figure 5 of Luu 2022.")
```

## Natural disease progression (sham)

Without treatment, BCVA declines from its baseline toward `gss` = 35.4 letters
with half-life `HL_kout` (Luu 2022 Eq 1 with C = 0). The ODE solution is
checked against the closed form
`g(t) = gss + (g0 - gss) * exp(-kout * t)`.

```{r sham}
sham_base <- c(EOP1003 = 51.3, EOP1004 = 54.0, MARINA = 53.6, PIER = 55.1)
ev_sham <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(sham_base), function(i) {
  make_arm(i, "sham", 0, NULL, sham_base[[i]], 104, obs_times = seq(0, 104, by = 2)) |>
    mutate(trial = names(sham_base)[i])
}))
sim_sham <- solve_typical(ev_sham, keep = "trial") |>
  as.data.frame()

closed <- sim_sham |>
  mutate(
    g0 = sham_base[trial],
    kout = log(2) / (21.6 * (g0 / 56.4)^2.57),
    g_closed = 35.4 + (g0 - 35.4) * exp(-kout * time)
  )
# Same parameters on both sides, so the difference is integrator error only.
stopifnot(max(abs(closed$bcva - closed$g_closed)) < 1e-3)

ggplot(sim_sham, aes(time, bcva_cfb, colour = trial)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Time (weeks)", y = "Change from baseline BCVA (letters)", colour = "Sham arm",
       caption = "Typical-value sham trajectories at the Table 2 baselines (compare Figure 2F of Luu 2022).")
```

## Between-arm variability

A stochastic simulation of 200 virtual ranibizumab 0.5 mg Q4 arms at the
median baseline (56.4 letters) shows the spread implied by the between-arm
variability on `HL_kout`, `Emax_ss` and `dEmax0`. The plotted quantity is
the arm-level prediction without residual error; for an arm of 300 subjects
the residual adds an SD of only 5.2 / sqrt(300) = 0.3 letters.

```{r vpc, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
ev_vpc <- bind_rows(lapply(1:200, function(i) {
  make_arm(i, "ranibizumab", 0.5, regimens$q4, 56.4, 52, obs_times = seq(0, 52, by = 2))
}))
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2022)
sim_vpc <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev_vpc) |> as.data.frame()

vpc <- sim_vpc |>
  group_by(time) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(bcva_cfb, 0.05),
    Q50 = quantile(bcva_cfb, 0.50),
    Q95 = quantile(bcva_cfb, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
typ <- solve_typical(filter(ev_vpc, id == 1)) |> as.data.frame()

# Centre only. A misplaced eta or a variance read as a CV shifts the median
# arm by several letters.
stopifnot(abs(vpc$Q50[vpc$time == 52] - typ$bcva_cfb[typ$time == 52]) < 2.5)

ggplot(vpc, aes(time, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_line(data = typ, aes(time, bcva_cfb), linetype = "dashed", colour = "blue") +
  labs(x = "Time (weeks)", y = "Change from baseline BCVA (letters)",
       caption = "Median and 90% interval of 200 simulated ranibizumab 0.5 mg Q4 arms; dashed: typical value.")
```

# PKNCA validation of the vitreous PK

The vitreous PK is one compartment with a fixed, drug-specific half-life. A
single labelled dose of each drug is checked with PKNCA. Cmax should equal
dose / 4 mL and the terminal half-life should equal the Table 1 value.

```{r pknca}
pk_dose <- c(ranibizumab = 0.5, aflibercept = 2, brolucizumab = 6, abicipar = 2)
ev_pk <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(pk_dose), function(i) {
  d <- names(pk_dose)[i]
  make_arm(i, d, pk_dose[[d]], 0, 56.4, 12, obs_times = c(0, 0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1:12)) |>
    mutate(treatment = d)
}))
sim_pk <- solve_typical(ev_pk, keep = "treatment") |>
  as.data.frame()

sim_nca <- sim_pk |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
dose_df <- ev_pk |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, time, amt, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id, route = "intravascular")
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
                        aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~cmax, ~half.life,
  "ranibizumab", 0.5 / 0.004, 1.29,
  "aflibercept", 2 / 0.004, 0.786,
  "brolucizumab", 6 / 0.004, 0.629,
  "abicipar", 2 / 0.004, 0.649
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "mg/L", half.life = "week"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated vitreous NCA vs. dose / 4 mL and the Table 1 half-lives. * differs by >20%.")

nca_tab <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "half.life")) |>
  select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  left_join(published, by = "treatment", suffix = c("_sim", "_ref"))
# Closed-form one-compartment PK, so only integration error separates the sides.
stopifnot(
  nrow(nca_tab) == 4,
  all(abs(nca_tab$cmax_sim / nca_tab$cmax_ref - 1) < 1e-3),
  all(abs(nca_tab$half.life_sim / nca_tab$half.life_ref - 1) < 1e-3)
)
```

The drug effect is driven by the vitreous concentration in nM,
`Cc * 1000 / MW(kDa)`. For example, 0.5 mg ranibizumab gives
125 mg/L / 48 kDa = `r round(125 * 1000 / 48)` nM, about 180 times its EC50
of 14.7 nM.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Molecular weights are not printed in Luu 2022.** EC50 values are in nM, so
  each vitreous concentration is converted from mg/L with the molecular
  weight of its drug. The maintainers took the weights from the sources the
  paper cites: ranibizumab ~48 kDa (Lucentis label), aflibercept 115 kDa
  including glycosylation (Eylea label, Luu 2022 ref 32), brolucizumab
  ~26 kDa (Beovu label) and abicipar 34 kDa (Callanan 2018, Luu 2022 ref 16).
  With these, the typical-value model reproduces the Figure 5 Q12
  predictions to within 0.7 letters.
- **Covariate centring.** The paper centres continuous covariates "on a
  typical value, eg, the median of the study population" but does not print
  the value. The model uses 56.4 letters, the median of the 55 arm baselines
  in Table 2.
- **Transform of the between-arm variability and form of the baseline
  covariate.** The paper models between-arm variability "as additive to
  logit-transformed parameters" and tests covariates "in log-space with a
  linear model". A logit needs no assumed bounds only for `Emax_ss` (0.842),
  so the maintainers ruled that `Emax_ss` is logit-normal, with the baseline
  covariate entering on the logit scale as `2.00 * log(SCORE_BCVA / 56.4)`.
  This keeps `Emax_ss` below 1 for every arm. `HL_kout` and `dEmax0` are
  log-normal, with a power covariate on `HL_kout`. The alternative reading, a
  multiplicative power `(SCORE_BCVA / 56.4)^2.00` on `Emax_ss`, gives
  typical-value Figure 4 predictions closer to the paper. It also gives
  Figure 5 Q12 predictions about 1.3 letters higher for brolucizumab and
  abicipar. Neither comparison decides between the readings, because the
  paper's figures average arm-specific empirical Bayes predictions rather
  than typical values. Arms whose baseline is far from 56.4 letters are the
  most sensitive to this choice.
- **Between-arm variability percentages** (99%, 9.35%, 118%) are read as
  100 times the standard deviation of the arm random effect on the
  transformed scale. A coefficient of variation is undefined on the logit
  scale, so the same reading is applied to all three.
- **Residual error.** The three additive SDs of Table 1 are used for sham
  arms, for treated arms up to week 52 and for treated arms after week 52.
  Each is divided by `sqrt(N_ARM)`, following "weighted by the square root of
  the number of subjects". `N_ARM` affects only the residual.
- **Time origin.** `t` in `exp(-kEmax * t)` is the time from the first dose
  (the x-axis of Figure 2), so event tables must start dosing at time 0.
- **Typical values, not empirical Bayes estimates.** The paper's Figures 4
  and 5 average predictions that use each arm's estimated random effects.
  Those estimates are not published, so this vignette compares typical-value
  predictions. Their across-arm SD reflects only the baseline-BCVA covariate.
- **Dosing schedules.** The arm regimens follow the Table 2 footnotes. For
  EXCITE and PIER Q12 the vignette uses three monthly loading doses, then
  quarterly dosing. For HAWK and HARRIER it uses three 4-weekly loading doses,
  then fixed Q12 dosing; the as-needed switches to Q8 are not reproduced. For
  Q8 regimens it uses three 4-weekly loading doses, then every 8 weeks. For
  abicipar Q12 it uses the Figure 5 schedule (weeks 0, 4, 12, then every 12
  weeks), which gives the same 5.92-letter prediction in Figures 4 and 5.
- **Bevacizumab** arms (BRAMD, CATT) were fitted with the ranibizumab EC50,
  but no bevacizumab half-life is reported, so bevacizumab is not supported.
  The paper excluded it from its own simulations.
- No erratum or correction notice for Luu 2022 was found as of 2026-10-16.
